Elliott |date=August 28, 2024 |title=How 538 is adjusting our election model for Harris versus Trump |url=https://abcnews.go.com/538/538-adjusting-election-model-harris-versus-trump/story?id=112563822 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240829084450/https://abcnews.go.com/538/538-adjusting-election-model-harris-versus-trump/story?id=112563822 |archive-date=August 29, 2024 |access-date=2024-08-29 |website=ABC News |language=en}}</ref>

Silver's final forecast for the election gave Trump and Harris almost an exactly even chance of winning the Electoral College (50.015% for Harris, 49.985% for Trump).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Silver |first=Nate |title=FINAL Silver Bulletin 2024 presidential election forecast |url=https://www.natesilver.net/p/nate-silver-2024-president-election-polls-model |access-date=July 18, 2024 |archive-date=July 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718071732/https://www.natesilver.net/p/nate-silver-2024-president-election-polls-model |url-status=live }}</ref> His model also forecast that a Trump victory in all seven swing states was the single most likely outcome (at over 20% likelihood),<ref>{{Cite news |last=Shoaib |first=Alia |title=Donald Trump's Chances of Winning a Landslide, According to Nate Silver |url=https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-landslide-nate-silver-1979693 |website=Newsweek |language=en |archive-date=November 9, 2024 |access-date=November 6, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241109163119/https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-landslide-nate-silver-1979693 |url-status=live }}</ref> and that a comfortable Electoral College victory of some form had better than even odds of occurring (with over 60% likelihood that one candidate would win at least six swing states).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Silver |first=Nate |title=Nate Silver: Here's What My Gut Says About the Election. But Don't Trust Anyone's Gut, Even Mine. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/23/opinion/election-polls-results-trump-harris.html |website=New York Times |date=October 23, 2024 |language=en |archive-date=November 6, 2024 |access-date=November 6, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241106120902/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/23/opinion/election-polls-results-trump-harris.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Trump won the Presidency and all seven swing states.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-10 |title=Why AP called Arizona for Trump |url=https://apnews.com/article/ap-race-call-explainer-arizona-president-5c3c3ea3d31ab8ebc4079ff2f7eab348 |access-date=2024-11-10 |website=AP News |language=en |archive-date=November 10, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241110044020/https://apnews.com/article/ap-race-call-explainer-arizona-president-5c3c3ea3d31ab8ebc4079ff2f7eab348 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Silver's final forecast also gave the advantage (i.e. greater than 50% odds of winning) to the eventual winner in 48 out of the 50 states, as well as the District of Columbia and all congressional districts awarding electoral votes.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Silver |first1=Nate |title=The model exactly predicted the most likely election map |url=https://www.natesilver.net/p/the-model-exactly-predicted-the-most |website=Silver Bulletin |access-date=7 November 2024 |archive-date=November 8, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241108040303/https://www.natesilver.net/p/the-model-exactly-predicted-the-most |url-status=live }}</ref> Only Trump's victories in Michigan and Wisconsin did not occur in the majority of Silver's final simulations.

==''The Signal and the Noise''==
{{main|The Signal and the Noise}}

[[File:Nate Silver at SXSW 2013.jpg|thumb|right|Silver signing a copy of ''The Signal and the Noise'' at [[South by Southwest|SXSW]] 2013]]

''The Signal and The Noise'' was published in the United States on September 27, 2012. It reached the [[New York Times Best Sellers List]] as #12 for non-fiction hardback books after its first week in print. It dropped to #20 in the second week, before rising to #13 in the third, and remaining on the non-fiction hardback top 15 list for the following 13 weeks, with a highest weekly ranking of #4.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cowles |first=Gregory |title=New York Times Best Sellers List |url=https://www.nytimes.com/best-sellers-books/hardcover-nonfiction/list.html |work=The New York Times |access-date=December 5, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131205214736/http://www.nytimes.com/best-sellers-books/hardcover-nonfiction/list.html |archive-date=December 5, 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref> Sales increased after the election on November 6, jumping 800% and becoming the second best seller on [[Amazon.com]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jason |last=Notte |title=Nate Silver sees soaring Amazon book sales: The FiveThirtyEight blogger's confident and steadfast Obama forecast gets readers curious and critics furious |url=http://money.msn.com/top-stocks/post.aspx?post=3d424e42-2010-4c0d-abed-340c55f00240&ocid=ansmony11 |work=[[MSN Money]] |date=November 8, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130115174458/http://money.msn.com/top-stocks/post.aspx?post=3d424e42-2010-4c0d-abed-340c55f00240&ocid=ansmony11 |archive-date=January 15, 2013 }}</ref>

The book describes methods of mathematical model-building using [[probability]] and statistics. Silver takes a big-picture approach to using statistical tools, combining sources of unique data (e.g., timing a minor league ball player's fastball using a radar gun), with historical data and principles of sound statistical analysis; Silver argues that many of these are violated by many pollsters and pundits who nonetheless have important media roles. Case studies in the book include baseball, elections, [[climate change]], the financial crash, poker, and weather forecasting. These different topics illustrate different statistical principles. As a reviewer in ''The New York Times'' notes: "It's largely about evaluating predictions in a variety of fields, from finance to weather to epidemiology. We learn about a handful of successes: when, for instance, meteorologists predict a hurricane's landfall 72 hours in advance.... But mostly we learn about failures. It turns out we're not even close to predicting the next catastrophic earthquake or the spread of the next killer bird flu, despite the enormous amounts of brainpower trained on these questions in the past few decades."<ref>{{cite news |first=Noam |last=Scheiber |title=Known Unknowns: ''The Signal and the Noise,'' by Nate Silver |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/11/04/books/review/the-signal-and-the-noise-by-nate-silver.html |date=November 2, 2012 |access-date=October 16, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161006220101/http://www.nytimes.com/2012/11/04/books/review/the-signal-and-the-noise-by-nate-silver.html |archive-date=October 6, 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Silver also appeared on ''[[The Colbert Report]]'' (October 7, 2008, and November 5, 2012),<ref>[http://www.colbertnation.com/the-colbert-report-videos/187343/october-07-2008/nate-silver Nate Silver on "Colbert Report" 2008] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218221050/http://www.colbertnation.com/the-colbert-report-videos/187343/october-07-2008/nate-silver |date=December 18, 2008 }} and [http://www.colbertnation.com/the-colbert-report-videos/420765/november-05-2012/nate-silver Nate Silver on "Colbert Report" 2012] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106131448/http://www.colbertnation.com/the-colbert-report-videos/420765/november-05-2012/nate-silver |date=November 6, 2012 }}.</ref> ''[[The Daily Show]]'' (October 17, 2012, and November 7, 2012),<ref>[http://www.thedailyshow.com/full-episodes/wed-october-17-2012-nate-silver Nate Silver on "The Daily Show"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121018204825/http://www.thedailyshow.com/full-episodes/wed-october-17-2012-nate-silver |date=October 18, 2012 }}.</ref> and ''[[Real Time with Bill Maher]]'' (October 26, 2012).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hbo.com/real-time-with-bill-maher/episodes/index.html#/real-time-with-bill-maher/episodes/0/264-episode/index.html |title=Real Time with Bill Maher |publisher=Hbo.com |access-date=December 5, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131214053343/http://www.hbo.com/real-time-with-bill-maher/episodes/index.html#/real-time-with-bill-maher/episodes/0/264-episode/index.html |archive-date=December 14, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Silver's first appearance on [[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] as Editor-in-Chief of the new ''FiveThirtyEight.com'' was on [[George Stephanopoulos]]'s ''[[This Week (ABC TV series)|This Week]]'' on November 3, 2013.<ref>{{cite news |date=2013-03-11 |title=Nate Silver on 'This Week' |url=https://abcnews.go.com/ThisWeek/video/espns-nate-silver-week-2014-election-picture-20770078 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131209192705/http://abcnews.go.com/ThisWeek/video/espns-nate-silver-week-2014-election-picture-20770078 |archive-date=December 9, 2013 |access-date=December 5, 2013 |publisher=ABC News}}</ref>

Silver is referenced in the [[Syfy channel]] show ''[[The Magicians (U.S. TV series)|The Magicians]]'' as an earth wizard who uses polling spells.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/the-magicians-season-2-episode-10-review-the-girl-who-told-time/|title=The Magicians Season 2 Episode 10 Review: The Girl Who Told Time|website=Den of Geek}}</ref>

In 2015, Silver appeared on the podcast ''[[Employee of the Month (podcast)|Employee of the Month]]'', where he criticized [[Vox Media]] for "recycling Wikipedia entries" in their content.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/erik-wemple/wp/2015/11/09/nate-silver-accuses-vox-of-recycling-wikipedia-entries/|title=Nate Silver accuses Vox of recycling Wikipedia entries|last=Wemple|first=Erik|date=November 9, 2015|newspaper=The Washington Post|access-date=November 14, 2019|archive-date=March 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210312151327/https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/erik-wemple/wp/2015/11/09/nate-silver-accuses-vox-of-recycling-wikipedia-entries/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Selected recognition and awards==
* April 30, 2009: Silver was named one of [[Time 100|"The World's 100 Most Influential People"]] by ''[[Time (magazine)|TIME]]'' magazine.<ref name="specials1" />
* May 12, 2013: Silver received an honorary [[Doctor of Science]] degree (''Scientiæ Doctor honoris causa'' – D.Sc. h.c.) and gave the commencement address at [[Ripon College (Wisconsin)|Ripon College]].<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E6GAKeFh8SE Ripon 2013 video] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160504010456/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E6GAKeFh8SE |date=May 4, 2016 }} of Ripon College honorary degree award and commencement speech.</ref>
* May 24, 2013: Silver received an honorary [[Doctor of Letters|Doctor of Literature]] degree (Doctor of Literature ''honoris causa'') and presented a commencement address at [[The New School]].<ref>[http://vimeo.com/67336820 New School 2013 commencement video] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203104703/http://vimeo.com/67336820 |date=February 3, 2014 }}.</ref>
* October 2013: Silver's ''The Signal and the Noise'' won the 2013 [[Phi Beta Kappa Award in Science]], which recognizes "outstanding contributions by scientists to the literature of science".<ref name="pbk.org">{{cite web |date=October 8, 2013 |title=Phi Beta Kappa book award in science |url=http://www.pbk.org/home/newsview.aspx?id=998 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131024041741/http://www.pbk.org/home/newsview.aspx?id=998 |archive-date=October 24, 2013 |access-date=December 5, 2013 |publisher=Pbk.org}}</ref>
* December 2013: The [[Katholieke Universiteit Leuven|University of Leuven (KU Leuven)]] (Belgium) and the Leuven Statistics Research Centre awarded Silver an honorary doctoral degree "for his prominent role in the development, application, and dissemination of proper prediction methods in sports and in political sciences".<ref>
"Honorary Doctorate for Nate Silver", [http://lstat.kuleuven.be/LStat25/Nate%20Silver.htm LStat: Leuven Statistics Research Centre] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20131204045244/http://lstat.kuleuven.be/LStat25/Nate%20Silver.htm |date=December 4, 2013 }} 
</ref><ref>
Luc Vander Elst, "Honorary doctorate for Nate Silver, the man who made statistics cool", KU Leuven, [http://www.kuleuven.be/english/news/honorary-doctorate-for-nate-silver-the-man-who-made-statistics-cool December 18, 2013] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224103042/http://www.kuleuven.be/english/news/honorary-doctorate-for-nate-silver-the-man-who-made-statistics-cool |date=December 24, 2013 }} 
</ref>
* May 25, 2014: Silver received a Doctorate of Humane Letters, ''honoris causa'', from [[Amherst College]].<ref>Honorary doctorate from Amherst, [https://www.amherst.edu/aboutamherst/news/specialevents/commencement/awards/2014-honorees/nate-silver 2014] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140527220605/https://www.amherst.edu/aboutamherst/news/specialevents/commencement/awards/2014-honorees/nate-silver |date=May 27, 2014 }}.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://photos.masslive.com/republican/2014/05/193rd_commencement_at_amherst_college_18.html|title=193rd Commencement at Amherst College|work=masslive.com|access-date=May 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140527215510/http://photos.masslive.com/republican/2014/05/193rd_commencement_at_amherst_college_18.html|archive-date=May 27, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*May 2017: Georgetown University awarded Silver a degree of Doctor of Humane Letters ''honoris causa''.<ref>[https://www.georgetown.edu/news/commencement-speakers-2017 "Georgetown Announces 2017 Commencement Speakers"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170517070642/https://www.georgetown.edu/news/commencement-speakers-2017 |date=May 17, 2017 }}.</ref>
*May 2018: Kenyon College awarded Silver a degree, Doctor of Humane Letters.<ref>[http://www.kenyon.edu/middle-path/for-the-media/media-relations/press-release-archives/kenyon-set-to-celebrate-190th-commencement-fivethirtyeight-editor-nate-silver-to-give-address/ Kenyon College honorary degree] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180520054900/http://www.kenyon.edu/middle-path/for-the-media/media-relations/press-release-archives/kenyon-set-to-celebrate-190th-commencement-fivethirtyeight-editor-nate-silver-to-give-address/ |date=May 20, 2018 }}.</ref>

==Personal life==
Silver is a great-nephew of geologists [[Caswell Silver]] and [[Leon Silver]]. He is a great-grandson of Harmon Lewis, the President of Alcoa Steamship Company,<ref>{{Cite news|first=Nate |last=Bloom |author-link=Nate Bloom   |title= Interfaith Celebrities: Nate Silver, Another Bond, and Happy Endings  |newspaper=[[InterfaithFamily]]|date= November 13, 2012 |url=http://www.interfaithfamily.com/arts_and_entertainment/popular_culture/Interfaith_Celebrities_Nate_Silver_Another_Bond_and_Happy_Endings.shtml  | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121121022651/http://www.interfaithfamily.com/arts_and_entertainment/popular_culture/Interfaith_Celebrities_Nate_Silver_Another_Bond_and_Happy_Endings.shtml| archive-date=November 21, 2012|quote=His mother is the granddaughter of the late Harmon Lewis, once head of the Alcoa Steamship Company. Silver's middle name is also the first name of a maternal great-aunt and the middle name of his mother's sister}}</ref> as well as a great-great-nephew of the embryologist [[Warren Harmon Lewis]] and his wife, biologist [[Margaret Reed Lewis]].{{citation needed|date=April 2017}}

Silver is [[gay]],<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Cadwalladr |first=Carole |date=2012-11-17 |title=Nate Silver: it's the numbers, stupid |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/nov/17/nate-silver-interview-election-data-statistics |access-date= |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> and lives with his longtime partner Robert Gauldin in [[Manhattan]].<ref>{{cite web|title=A $3M NoHo condo wins over elections guru Nate Silver|url=https://www.crainsnewyork.com/real-estate/residential/cny-nate-silver-buys-noho-condo-20260501/|date=May 1, 2026|first=C. J.|last=Hughes|website=Crain’s New York Business}}</ref> "I've always felt like something of an outsider. I've always had friends but I've always come from an outside point of view. I think that's important. If you grow up gay or in a household that's agnostic when most people are religious, then from the get-go, you are saying there are things the majority of society believes that I don't believe", he told an interviewer in 2012.<ref name=":2" /> When asked "what made you feel more of a misfit, being gay or being a geek", he replied, "Probably the numbers stuff since I had that from when I was six."<ref name=":2" /> When asked in 2008 if he had noticed people looking at him as a "gay icon", he responded, "I've started to notice it a little bit although so far it seems like I'm more a subject of geek affection than gay affection".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grant |first=Japhy |date=2008-11-21 |title=Nate Silver on African-Americans, Prop 8. and Being A Hero to Gays & Geeks Everywhere |url=https://www.queerty.com/exclusive-nate-silver-on-african-americans-prop-8-and-being-a-hero-to-gays-geeks-everywhere-20081121/ |access-date= |website=Queerty |language=en}}</ref>

Silver discussed his sexuality in the context of growing up in East Lansing in an article about the [[U.S. Supreme Court|Supreme Court]] ruling ''[[Obergefell v. Hodges]]'' in favor of recognizing [[same-sex marriage]] on the date of its announcement. He analyzed the speed of the change of public sentiment, pointing out that the change over only several decades has been palpable to the current generations.<ref name="2015-06-26_Silver">[https://web.archive.org/web/20171018225235/https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/change-doesnt-usually-come-this-fast/ Change Doesn't Usually Come This Fast], Nate Silver, ''[[FiveThirtyEight]]'', June 26, 2015, accessed June 29, 2015</ref>

Silver has long been interested in [[fantasy baseball]], especially Scoresheet Baseball. While in college he served as an expert on Scoresheet Baseball for [[Ron Shandler|BaseballHQ]].<ref>Zak Stambor, "Number Cruncher", [http://magazine.uchicago.edu/0878/features/nate_silver.shtml ''University of Chicago Magazine'', July–August, 2008] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080721011512/http://magazine.uchicago.edu/0878/features/nate_silver.shtml |date=July 21, 2008 }}.</ref> When he took up political writing, Silver abandoned his blog, ''The Burrito Bracket'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.burritobracket.blogspot.com/|title=BurritoBracket.com|publisher=Burritobracket.blogspot.com|date=February 23, 2004|access-date=August 21, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130114195034/http://burritobracket.blogspot.com/|archive-date=January 14, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> in which he ran a one-and-done competition among the taquerias in his [[Wicker Park, Chicago|Wicker Park]] neighborhood in Chicago.<ref>On the role of ''The Burrito Bracket'' in Silver's engagement in blogging see Dan Cohen, "The Ivory Tower and the Open Web: Introduction: Burritos, Browsers and Books", [http://www.dancohen.org/2011/07/26/the-ivory-tower-and-the-open-web-introduction-burritos-browsers-and-books-draft/ Dan Cohen's ''Digital Humanities'' blog, July 26, 2011] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110810001104/http://www.dancohen.org/2011/07/26/the-ivory-tower-and-the-open-web-introduction-burritos-browsers-and-books-draft/ |date=August 10, 2011 }}. [retrieved August 6, 2011]</ref>

Silver plays [[poker]] semi-professionally.<ref name=chicagotribune/><ref name=poker>{{cite web|title=This Post Brought to You by Poker|url=https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/this-post-brought-to-you-by-poker/|publisher=[[FiveThirtyEight]]|last=Silver|first=Nate|date=July 2, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121126021614/http://www.fivethirtyeight.com/2009/07/this-post-brought-to-you-by-poker.html|archive-date=November 26, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> He has $981,884 in total tournament earnings,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nate Silver's profile on The Hendon Mob |url=https://pokerdb.thehendonmob.com/player.php?a=r&n=283302 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230713015313/https://pokerdb.thehendonmob.com/player.php?a=r&n=283302 |archive-date=July 13, 2023 |access-date=December 30, 2023 |website=The Hendon Mob Poker Database |language=en}}</ref> including an 87th place finish in the 2023 [[World Series of Poker]] Main Event.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Paul |first=Tony |date=2023-07-13 |title=Michigan men out of WSOP Main Event; East Lansing's Nate Silver suffers a cooler |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/2023/07/13/michigan-men-out-of-wsop-main-event-east-lansings-nate-silver-suffers-a-cooler/70408871007/ |access-date= |website=The Detroit News |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Political views===
In a 2012 interview with [[Charlie Rose]], Silver said, "I'd say I'm somewhere in between being a [[libertarian]] and a [[liberalism|liberal]]. So if I were to vote, it would be kind of a [[Gary Johnson]] versus [[Mitt Romney]] decision, I suppose."<ref>{{cite episode |title=Mark Halperin of Time magazine and Nate Silver of FiveThirtyEight.com on the Presidential election |url=http://www.charlierose.com/watch/60140283 |series=[[Charlie Rose (TV series)|Charlie Rose]] |first=Charlie (host) |last=Rose |network=[[PBS]] |date=October 29, 2012 |access-date=October 6, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130926073817/http://charlierose.com/watch/60140283 |archive-date=September 26, 2013 }}</ref> In a 2023 newsletter, Silver said that he misspoke during that interview and meant to say that he would have chosen between Johnson and [[Barack Obama]]. He added that he has voted for the Democratic candidate in every presidential election he has participated in, though he registered as a Republican and voted for [[John Kasich]] in the [[2016 New York Republican presidential primary]] as he believed "the difference between a Kasich-led GOP and a Trump-led GOP would make a big difference to the future of the country".<ref name = Disagree>{{Cite web |last=Silver |first=Nate |date=September 12, 2023 |title=Not everyone who disagrees with you is a closet right-winger |url=https://www.natesilver.net/p/not-everyone-who-disagrees-with-you |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230912224615/https://www.natesilver.net/p/not-everyone-who-disagrees-with-you |archive-date=September 12, 2023 |access-date=September 13, 2023 |website=Silver Bulletin}}</ref>

Silver has also criticized "the progressive [[political class]]", believing that it has become "more ''[[left-wing politics|left]]'' and less ''liberal''".<ref name = Disagree/> In 2024, he said that he voted for [[Kathy Hochul]] in the [[2022 New York gubernatorial election]] and [[Kamala Harris]] in the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]], but has also criticized some of the Democratic Party's actions and political positions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.natesilver.net/p/sbsq-15-democrats-have-a-fool-me|title=SBSQ #15: Democrats have a "fool me twice" problem|access-date=December 17, 2024|date=November 26, 2024|website=Silver Bulletin|first1=Nate|last1=Silver|archive-date=December 13, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241213003441/https://www.natesilver.net/p/sbsq-15-democrats-have-a-fool-me|url-status=live}}</ref>
